Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, here is a synthesized answer to the user's question:

Parents often struggle to recall and understand their child's weight status information after a Body Mass Index (BMI) screening. While parents may remember that their child has a higher BMI than recommended, they may not be able to recall much of the specific advice provided about the result.

It is essential for healthcare providers to take extra steps to educate patients on what was discussed during the initial consultation and to follow up with them regularly to reinforce the information. This can include providing written information sheets or using nurse home visits to check in with parents and answer any questions they may have.

By taking a proactive approach, healthcare providers can help parents understand their child's weight status and make informed decisions about their care.
